thread.title: Yahoo Finance's market update: Dec. 4, 2018

author: Emily McCormick
title: Yahoo Finance's market update: Dec. 4, 2018
text:
U.S. stocks edged lower as optimism for a trade war resolution began to fade.
The S&P 500 ( ^GSPC ) fell 0.2%, or 5.48 points, as of 9:37 a.m. ET. The Dow ( ^DJI ) slipped 0.33%, or 86.33 points, while the Nasdaq ( ^IXIC ) fell 0.37%, or 27.32 points.
Equities posted a strong start to the month despite the downturn Tuesday morning. Investors’ risk appetite increased Monday after President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping’s meeting over the weekend at the G20 summit produced a 90-day halt to new tariffs , tempering some concern over trade tensions between the U.S. and China.
The start-of-the-month strength in equities is not unprecedented, as December has historically produced solid returns for stocks. Since 1950, no month has had a higher average return or been higher more often than the month of December, Ryan Detrick, LPL senior market strategist, said in an email.
“Although the well-known Santa Claus rally is technically the last five days of the year and the first two of the new year, you can’t deny the fact that December tends to bring with it good vibes and stocks gains,” Detrick said. “Given that the worst month this year was October with its 6.9% drop, history would say not to expect a similar big drop to end 2018.”
S&P 500 index monthly performance, 1950-2017 更多 The bond market, however, began the month by flashing a recessionary warning sign . An inversion of part of the U.S. Treasury yield curve occurred for the first time since 2007 on Monday, with the yield on the 5-year Treasury note falling below the yield on the 3-year note. An inversion also occurred between the yields on the 2- and 5-year notes, meaning that investors were paid more to hold the U.S. government debt with the shorter maturity.
However, the difference between the closely monitored 2- and 10-year yields remains upwardly sloped. An inversion of the 2- and the 10-year yield has preceded every U.S. recession since World War II. As of Tuesday morning, the difference between the 2-year yield at 2.827% and 10-year yield at 2.955% was about 13 basis points.
STOCKS: Apple gets downgraded again, homebuilder Toll Brothers reports decline in orders HSBC downgraded shares of Apple ( AAPL ) to Hold from Buy and cut the price target to $200 from $205. The firm cited moderating iPhone volume and value growth as reasons for the downgrade, adding, “While U.S. markets should remain solid, emerging markets, FX and diversification are headwinds in the short term. Growth in services could be a catalyst for the long term. Valuation looks undemanding, but catalysts are lacking.” Apple has continued to see its stock downgraded by the likes of Bank of America Merrill Lynch, Guggenheim and other firms recently on concerns of weak demand and macroeconomic headwinds. Shares of Apple fell 2.16% to $180.83 each as of 9:36 a.m. ET.
Traders work on the floor of the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE) in New York, U.S., December 3, 2018. REUTERS/Brendan McDermid 更多 Toll Brothers ( TOL ) reported a drop in quarterly orders for the first time in more than four years, overshadowing solid quarterly results for revenue and earnings. The luxury homebuilder said orders, which point to future revenue, dropped 13% to 1,715 units for the three months ending in October, whereas consensus expectations had been for an increase of 6.5%. Net income rose to $311 million, or $2.08 per share, beating estimates of $1.83 per share. Revenue came in at $2.46 billion, surging ahead of Wall Street’s expectations of $2.35 billion. Shares of Toll Brothers fell 9.19% to $30.45 each as of 9:36 a.m. ET.
